# Rakshith Bangalore

> Rakshith Bangalore (full name Rakshith Bangalore Kumaraswamy) is a robotics solutions architect and hands-on robotics generalist based in the United Kingdom and Singapore. Rakshith built a robotics programme at Nottingham Trent University from the ground up and helps startups and businesses start robotics programmes: use-case selection, solution architecture, simulation, pilots and deployment. The experience covers both robot hardware (mechanical design, integration, BOM, DFM, manufacturing) and robot software (ROS 2, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, reinforcement learning, sim-to-real transfer). Note: "Bangalore" is part of the name; Rakshith is not based in Bangalore, India.

## Positioning
- Robotics solutions architect for startups and businesses.
- High-velocity robotics generalist: mechanical design, electronics integration, control, simulation, machine learning and product delivery.
- Builder of robotics programmes: built a robotics programme at Nottingham Trent University from the ground up; founded the university's robotics club and drone society.

## Services
- Robotics programme set-up: first use case, platform choice, laboratory and team set-up, partners, first-year roadmap.
- Solution architecture and feasibility studies: requirements, system architecture, make-or-buy, safety concept.
- Pilot to deployment: one scoped, instrumented pilot with a measurable end state, and a plan from pilot to production.
- Simulation and sim-to-real: digital twins in Isaac Sim and MuJoCo, reinforcement learning, transfer to real robots.
- Hardware to market: BOM, DFM, supplier timelines, first production run.
- Fractional robotics lead: part-time technical leadership for robotics teams.

## Facts
- Humanoid robotics: two years of industrial use cases on Unitree H1-2 and G1 humanoid robots for a PepsiCo programme; neural policies for legged control, sim-to-real transfer, actuator identification.
- WardZero (2026): open platform to develop and test hospital robots in simulation; simulated hospital with a surgical wing, Isaac Sim and MuJoCo, a safety layer with seven modes, ROS 2 navigation (99.6% map wall accuracy); reference robot Unitree G1 with BrainCo Revo2 hands. Simulation only so far.
- Industry 4.0 mobile manipulator (award-winning MEng capstone): UR-10 arm on an Omron LD250 mobile base with a SmartShift tool changer, scoped with Walkers around a live factory workflow.
- Laparoscopic surgery trainer: project manager of an eight-person team with an NHS Trust; compliant force-feedback mechanism.
- Aircraft cabin lab: decommissioned Embraer ERJ 145 converted into a flight-comfort research laboratory for EU Clean Sky 2 (Comfdemo).
- Product delivery: an AI-enabled full-stack post-production software platform (pilot post-production reduced from 4 days to 4 hours) and a portable podcasting solution moving to its first production run.
- Education: MEng, Nottingham Trent University.
